item.description:
September 10, 2026 — 7:00 PM
Blue Llama Jazz Club

Thurs | Sep 10 Doors 5:30pm | Dinner 6pm | Show 8:30pm | $125 Ticket RESERVE TABLE(opens in new tab) About the Artist Enjoy a special five-course collaboration dinner from Blue LLama and Two James Spirits, capped off by a live set from Evening Star! 5:30pm – Doors 6:00pm – Five-course dinner, each course paired with a Two James cocktail 8:30pm – Evening Star takes the stage Evening Star is led by Detroit drummer Tariq Gardner, playing music of the African Diaspora – jazz, neo-soul, Afro-Cuban, spirituals, and hip-hop – with an Afro-futuristic sound built on original compositions and reworked classics from the Black American songbook. The group were 2025 finalists in WDET’s Sounds Like Detroit showcase and continue to tour nationally behind their releases Gateway Drug and Vice Tape. $125 includes five courses, five drink pairings, and your music cover. About the Menu Five courses, each paired with a Two James Spirits cocktail: Hamachi Crudo – umeboshi, cucumber paired with: Old Cockney Gin “Tonic” Seared Scallop – fennel, bouillabaisse sauce paired with: Nain Rouge Absinthe “Chrysanthemum” Duck Breast – roasted pineapple, vanilla paired with: Dr. Bird Rum “Daiquiri” Gail Force Citrus Gin sorbet intermezzo Grilled New York Strip – Stoney Creek Farms mushrooms paired with: J. Riddle Peated Bourbon “Boulevardier” Opera Cake paired with: Coffee Liqueur “Martini” About the Artist Evening Star is a Space Odyssey led by Detroit Drummer Tariq Gardner. The group has its roots in Detroit’s expansive musical tradition, blending the city’s rich Jazz legacy with its history of musicians being largely malleable to fit into a wide array of musical styles traveling to the different galaxies of music of the African Diaspora (jazz, neo-soul, Afro-Cuban, spirituals, hip-hop, etc.). Evening Star brings listeners light years into the cosmos while staying true to the roots of the Motherland. The band has an afro-futuristic aesthetic with the mission that simply makes music the forefront of positive outlets with original compositions as well as arrangements on popular songs from the Black American Canon. In 2025, they became finalists in NPR Detroit’s ( WDET) Sounds Like Detroit contest and music Showcase. Evening Star currently has two releases: Their 2023 freshman project, “Gateway Drug,” and their 2024 Sophomore project, “Vice Tape,” featuring poet Joel “Fluent” Greene. They are currently performing festivals nationwide and looking forward to the recording of their third release. item.title: Tyreek McDole @ Blue Llama Jazz Club
item.description:
September 11, 2026 — 7:00 PM
Blue Llama Jazz Club

Fri | Sep 11 Sets 7pm & 9pm $95 Dinner & Show $50 Cover Only RESERVE TABLE About the Artist Tyreek McDole is a multi-award-winning Haitian-American vocalist from Central Florida whose soulful baritone and deeply reflective artistry are making waves across the New York and international music scenes. Rooted in the belief that music is one of the highest forms of communication, McDole approaches performance as a space for healing, reflection, and collective dreaming – treating each concert as both offering and ritual. He first gained national recognition at the 2018 Essentially Ellington Competition at Jazz at Lincoln Center, where he received the Outstanding Vocalist Award presented by Wynton Marsalis. In 2023, he won first place at the prestigious Sarah Vaughan International Jazz Vocal Competition, becoming only the second male winner in the competition’s history and joining the ranks of standout vocalists such as Samara Joy. Since then, McDole has shared the stage with Jeff Goldblum, Rodney Whitaker, Theo Croker, Maurice Brown, Joey Alexander, Terri Lyne Carrington, Nicholas Payton, and Nick Jonas, among many others, and has appeared at leading venues and festivals worldwide. A graduate of the Oberlin Conservatory of Music, he developed his craft under the mentorship of master artists such as Gary Bartz, Sullivan Fortner and Weedie Braimah, grounding his sound in the lineage of Black American Music while pushing its language forward. His critically acclaimed debut album, Open Up Your Senses, blends original compositions with freedom songs, spirituals, and works that speak to justice, unity, and ancestral memory. The record reached #1 on JazzWeek charts, earned four stars from DownBeat, and has been praised for its emotional depth and spiritual resonance. With a voice steeped in warmth, gravity, and soul, McDole creates performances that are both intimate and expansive – honoring tradition while inviting listeners toward reflection, healing, and shared imagination. This is not simply a concert, but a healing space – a ritual and an invitation to open your senses. He wishes you peace, love, and light. RESERVE TABLE

item.title: Vincent Chandler Experience @ Blue Llama Jazz Club
item.description:
September 18, 2026 — 7:00 PM
Blue Llama Jazz Club

Fri | Sep 18 Sets 7pm & 9pm | $25 Cover RESERVE TABLE(opens in new tab) About the Artist Vincent Chandler is an American jazz trombonist, composer, arranger, educator, conductor, and scat singer from Detroit, Michigan. He is recognized as one of the leading figures in Detroit’s contemporary jazz scene and has built a career that combines performance, teaching, composition, and jazz preservation. Chandler earned both a Bachelor of Fine Arts in Jazz Studies and a Master of Music in Improvisation from the University of Michigan, where he studied with notable jazz artists including Donald Walden and Geri Allen. He has taught jazz at several universities, including Michigan State University, the University of Michigan, Claflin University, South Carolina State University, and currently serves as an Assistant Professor and Area Coordinator of Jazz Studies at Wayne State University. As a performer, Chandler has appeared with many of the world’s leading jazz artists, including Herbie Hancock, Wynton Marsalis, Roy Hargrove, Joe Henderson, Marcus Miller, Ambrose Akinmusire, James Carter, Geri Allen, Robert Hurst, Rodney Whitaker and JD Allen. His touring has taken him throughout North America, Europe, Asia, Australia, New Zealand, Central America, Mexico, and the Caribbean. Chandler has recorded as both a leader and sideman. His recordings include the album Embraceable and featured performances on Roy Hargrove’s Emergence, James Carter’s At the Crossroads, and Carl Allen and Rodney Whitaker’s Work to Do. Beyond performing and teaching, Chandler is a dedicated advocate for Detroit’s jazz heritage. He founded the Detroit Jazz Preservation Concert Series, an initiative that celebrates the city’s influential jazz musicians and history. In recognition of his artistic contributions, he received a 2020 Kresge Arts in Detroit Artist Fellowship and he received The Living Legacy Award for his outstanding leadership, service and dedication from The Carr Center & Urban Art Orchestra in 2025. He is a core member of Don Was and the Pan-Detroit Ensemble, the Detroit-based group assembled by Don Was to celebrate the city’s rich musical traditions through a blend of jazz, funk, blues, soul, and R&B. Within the Pan-Detroit Ensemble, Chandler is one of the band’s featured soloists and music arranger for the horn section, helping shape the band’s rich brass sound. Don Was and the Pan-Detroit Ensemble’s debut album, Groove in the Face of Adversity, was released in 2025. He was also featured in the ensemble’s 2026 Tiny Desk Concert. Lineup: Vincent Chandler – trombone, vocals Zach Sommerfield – Guitar Jacob Hart – Piano Michael Abbo – bass David Ward – drums RESERVE TABLE(opens in new tab)

Sat | Sep 19 Sets at 7pm and 8:30pm | $25 Cover RESERVE TABLE About the Artist David Janeway’s musical journey began in the heart of Detroit in the early sixties, where he was deeply influenced by the Motown sound and local jazz legends like Marcus Belgrave and Harold McKinney. In 1978, he moved to New York City, where he further honed his craft and collaborated with a myriad of remarkable artists, from The Supremes to Art Farmer, Sonny Fortune, Billy Hart, Angel Canales and Sabor, Craig Handy, Gary Smulyan, Eliot Zigmund and many more. Janeway has left an indelible mark on the New York City jazz scene, performing with his trio and quintet at renowned venues like Smalls, Mezzrow, Zinc Bar, Sweet Basil, Birdland, Django and more. He’s also taken his music to a global stage, gracing the Detroit Jazz Festival, Madison Square Garden, the Village Gate, and numerous clubs and venues across the US and Europe. Janeway recently released his album David Janeway Trio Live at Blue LLama. Captured live at Ann Arbor, Michigan’s renowned jazz club Blue Llama in June 2024, David Janeway presents himself at the height of his powers, joined by the world-class rhythm team of Robert Hurst III and Billy Hart. A Detroit-bred musician with a deep lineage in that city’s storied jazz tradition, Janeway channels decades of mentorship, swing, and blues-rooted expression into a set that is both powerfully modern and historically grounded. The trio’s telepathic interplay fuels inventive takes on standards, luminous ballads, and Janeway’s distinctive originals, all delivered with the group’s tightly converging sound and emotional depth that define his artistry. Following acclaimed SteepleChase releases with Hart and Cameron Brown, this live recording stands as Janeway’s most vibrant statement yet-an inspired document of three master musicians creating in the moment. RESERVE TABLE

item.title: Pandit Partha Bose + Pandit Samar Saha @ Blue Llama Jazz Club
item.description:
September 20, 2026 — 7:00 PM
Blue Llama Jazz Club

Sun | Sep 20 Set 7pm | $25 Cover RESERVE TABLE(opens in new tab) About the Artist About Pandit Partha Bose A leading light of the Maihar Gharana, Pandit Partha Bose is a master Sitarist whose artistry bridges ancient tradition and modern expression. To understand Bose is to appreciate the “jazz” of India-his performances are masterclasses in raga (melodic framework) and improvisation, built on a foundation of rigorous technical discipline. Trained under the legacy of Ustad Allauddin Khan, Bose is renowned for his ability to weave complex, meditative tapestries of sound that resonate with deep emotional intelligence. A veteran of the world’s most prestigious stages, he offers an experience that is as intellectually demanding as it is profoundly soulful. About Samar Saha Pandit Samar Saha is a titan of the Tabla-the intricate, virtuosic hand drums that form the rhythmic heartbeat of Hindustani classical music. A master of time and nuance, Saha commands a rhythmic vocabulary that rivals the most sophisticated modern percussionists. Hailing from the historic musical center of Kolkata, his playing is defined by a lightning-fast precision and an uncanny ability to engage in complex rhythmic dialogues with his fellow musicians. Whether serving as a sensitive accompanist or a commanding soloist, Saha’s performance is a display of pure technical brilliance and rhythmic invention that captivates listeners of any genre. About Hindustani Classical Music & Jazz Hindustani classical music is a meditative, improvisational tradition that has long shared a deep, soulful resonance with Western jazz. For decades, this exchange has captivated audiences, built on a common language of spontaneous creation, intricate rhythmic structures, and a quest for spiritual depth. This cross-cultural fascination became a defining movement in the 1960s, famously sparked by the legendary collaboration between Ravi Shankar and John Coltrane. Coltrane saw in Shankar’s raga system a framework for his own explorations into modal jazz and transcendence, directly influencing works like Africa/Brass and his pursuit of “universal” sounds. Simultaneously, the global spotlight on Indian classical music was amplified by The Beatles-most notably George Harrison-who integrated the haunting timbre of the sitar into the pop lexicon, introducing millions of Western listeners to the hypnotic, microtonal beauty of Indian ragas. Today, this dialogue remains vibrant, as modern jazz masters continue to draw from the Hindustani well of rhythmic complexity and melodic fluidity. When Pandit Partha Bose and Pandit Samar Saha take the stage, they are not merely performing an ancient tradition; they are continuing a storied, high-level musical conversation-one that invites the jazz-savvy listener to lose themselves in the same sense of wonder that has bridge Eastern tradition and Western innovation for generations. Wed | Sep 23 Set 7pm $85 Dinner & Show $40 Cover Only RESERVE TABLE(opens in new tab) About the Artist Nicole Zuraitis is a 2X GRAMMY® winning and 6X GRAMMY-nominated jazz singer-songwriter, producer, pianist, arranger, New York-based bandleader and winner of the prestigious American Traditions Vocal Competition Gold Medal. With a “heart as big as her remarkable voice,” (Jazz Police), Nicole has positioned herself as one of the top artists and “prolific songwriters” (Broadway World) to watch in jazz and beyond, or as she likes to call it, The Modern Songbook. As a recording artist, Nicole has released seven albums as leader, and her sixth album, How Love Begins, co-produced with eight-time GRAMMY-winner Christian McBride, won BEST JAZZ VOCAL ALBUM at the 2024 GRAMMY® awards and features all original music. She is the only person ever to have won this award who wrote and arranged the entire album herself. Her live album Live at Vic’s Las Vegas, which she produced, wrote and arranged  featuring Tom Scott, Keyon Harrold, Rachel Eckroth, Idan Morim, Sam Weber and Dan Pugach, was nominated for 2 GRAMMYS in 2026.  She will release her next studio album The Devil I Knew, produced by Larry Klein, in July of 2026. In addition to leading her quartet, Nicole performed and recorded with the Birdland Big Band as the premier vocalist before taking off as a large ensemble leader of her own, co-producing the Dan Pugach Big Band and guesting for major big bands around the globe.  She has headlined at Newport Jazz Festival, Melbourne International Jazz Festival, Caramoor, Saratoga Jazz Festival and Tanglewood, along with iconic NYC jazz clubs like Dizzy’s Club at Lincoln Center, Birdland, the Blue Note, the Carlyle, 54 Below and the late, great 55 Bar. She also has appeared as a featured soloist with the Savannah Philharmonic, Asheville Symphony, and Macon Pops as well as the Danish Radio Big Band. Her original song “Always” closed the 2025 Teyana Taylor GRAMMY Nominated album Escape Room (Def Jam Records). Nicole is a featured artist and producer on her husband’s, renowned drummer, bandleader, and composer Dan Pugach, 2025 GRAMMY-winning album, Bianca Reimagined: Music for Paws and Persistence (Best Large Ensemble) for which they composed the GRAMMY-nominated song, “Little Fears” (Best Jazz Performance). Nicole is a vocalist on the GRAMMY-winning “Last Sunday in Plains: A Centennial Celebration” alongside Jon Batiste, Keb’ Mo’, and LeeAnn Rimes. In 2024, Broadway World honored Nicole with the “Best Big Band Show” Award. Nicole’s arrangement of Dolly Parton’s Jolene, co-written with Dan Pugach, was nominated for a 2019 GRAMMY®, springboarding her career and making her a household name in the modern-day jazz landscape. In 2020, she was named in the top 40 under 40 for 2020 in Connecticut Magazine, and her weekly live stream during the Covid-19 crisis, “Virtual Piano Lounge,” was featured in Forbes Magazine. Her Live at Vic’s Las Vegas album was featured on NPR Toast of the Nation 2026 in an hour long special.  Nicole has collaborated with an extensive list of luminaries, including Christian McBride, Tom Scott, Keyon Harrold, David Cook, Larry Klein, Gilad Hekselman, Veronica Swift, Benny Benack, Stephen Feifke, Cyrille Aimee, Antonio Sanchez, Javon Jackson, Nikki Giovanni, Dave Stryker, Omar Hakim,  Rachel Z, Helen Sung, Melanie, Morgan James, Darren Criss, Livingston Taylor, Thana Alexa, Rachel Eckroth, Don Braden and Bernard Purdie. She is a proud educator and a current vocal faculty member at NYU and the Litchfield Jazz Camp. In 2024, Post University awarded Nicole an Honorary Doctorate in Humane Letters. An ardent activist with a decade-long track record of giving back, her release of How Love Begins coincided with a self-produced music festival and day of activism for SavetheSound.Org. item.description:
September 27, 2026 — 7:00 PM
Blue Llama Jazz Club

Sun | Sep 27 Sets at 6pm and 7:30pm | $25 Cover RESERVE TABLE About the Artist Women in Jazz ShowcaseFeaturing Pamela Wise, Lady Vonne & Naima Shambourger Join us for an elegant evening celebrating the powerhouse women of jazz. The performance features an extraordinary rhythm section with Pamela Wise on piano, Laura Simone on bass, and Gayelynn McKinney on drums. The showcase highlights two exceptional vocal sets. Opening the evening at 6:00 PM is Naima Shambourger. Praised as a modern heir to Sarah Vaughan’s legacy, Ms. Shambourger delivers a masterful presence shaped by classical training, a deep jazz lineage, and heartfelt phrasing. At 7:30 PM, the stage welcomes Lady Vonne, a renowned Detroit jazz, R&B, and soul vocalist celebrated for her glamorous stage presence and timeless voice. About NaimaNaima Shamborguer was born and raised in Detroit Michigan. Born to a musical family, professional musicians surrounded her. From her early days of musical training, Naima developed highly artistic and finely polished vocal abilities through extensive training in classical and jazz music, but jazz music is where Naima has made a successful career. On two occasions Naima received The Spirit of Detroit award from the City Council of Detroit. Recognizing the exceptional achievement, outstanding leadership, and dedication to improving the quality of life and “The Women in Jazz.” The late Hugh Lawson deemed her “the closest that he has ever heard to Sarah Vaughan, all she needs is to be heard.” Inducted into the Kresge Fellow program in 2020. And with performances ranging from the Blue Llama in Ann Arbor to the Peacock Jazz Café in Toledo, Ohio and back up to the Dirty Dog Jazz Café in Detroit, MI. About Lady VonneLady Vonne (born Yvonne Dowell) is an acclaimed jazz, R&B, and standards vocalist based in Detroit, Michigan. Often described as a musical blend of Ella Fitzgerald, Phyllis Hyman, and Diana Ross, she is highly regarded as one of Detroit’s premier jazz greats. About Pamela WiseBuilding upon the Detroit jazz connection established with Lady Vonne, Pamela Wise (also known as Pamela Wise Harrison) is an acclaimed contemporary jazz pianist, composer, and educator based in Detroit, Michigan. She is highly revered for her unique style that fuses post-bop jazz with fiery Afro-Cuban and West African rhythms. About Gayelynn McKinneyContinuing the deep exploration of Detroit’s iconic jazz legacy, Gayelynn McKinney is one of the most decorated, formidable, and trailblazing drummers in the history of the Detroit jazz scene. With a career spanning multiple decades, she has served as a master rhythmist, composer, educator, and a crucial anchor for women in percussion. About Laura SimoneContinuing the thread of exceptional women in jazz, Laura Simone is a rising 20-year-old jazz bassist, vocalist, and activist. Originally from Lawrenceville, New Jersey, she is currently a junior at Michigan State University studying under the mentorship of renowned bassist Rodney Whitaker. RESERVE TABLE

Thu | Oct 1 Sets 7pm & 8:30pm | $25 Cover Reserve Table About the Artist Ellen Rowe, jazz pianist and composer, is currently Arthur F. Thurnau Professor of Jazz and Contemporary Improvisation at the University of Michigan. She is a graduate of the Eastman School of Music, where she studied with Rayburn Wright and Bill Dobbins.  Prior to her appointment in Michigan, she served as Director of Jazz Studies at the University of Connecticut. Winner of the Hartford, CT Advocate Readers’ Poll for Best Acoustic Jazz, Ms. Rowe has performed at jazz clubs and on concert series throughout the U.S., as well as touring in Germany, Holland, Switzerland, Ireland, Poland, South Africa and Australia. CDs out under her own name include “Sylvan Way”, “Wishing Well”, “Denali Pass” and “Courage Music.”  Her latest project, “Momentum – Portraits of Women In Motion”, featuring Ingrid Jensen, Tia Fuller, Marion Hayden and Allison Miller was released in January of 2019. Also active as a clinician, she has given workshops and master classes at the Melbourne Conservatory, Hochshule fur Musik in Cologne, Grieg Academy in Bergen and the Royal Academy of Music in London, in addition to many appearances as a guest artist at festivals and Universities around the country. When not leading her own trio, quartet or quintet, she is in demand as a sideman, having performed with a wide variety of jazz artists including Kenny Wheeler, Tim Ries, Tom Harrell, John Clayton, Ingrid Jensen and Steve Turre.  She was also a guest on two installments of Marian McPartland’s  “Piano Jazz” on National Public Radio. Ms. Rowe’s compositions and arrangements have been performed and recorded by jazz ensembles and orchestras around the world, including the Village Vanguard Orchestra, BBC Jazz Orchestra, U.S. Navy Commodores, Berlin and NDR Radio Jazz Orchestras, London Symphony, DIVA and the Perth Jazz Orchestra.  Many of these works can be heard on recordings including “Leave It To DIVA”, “The Perth Jazz Orchestra”, “Bingo” (The Bird of Paradise Orchestra) and “I Believe In You” (DIVA). She has recently been a composer-in-residence at the Eastman School of Music and the University of Wisconsin at Madison.  Recent jazz ensemble commissions include the Minnesota Band Directors Association, Belleville (MI) High School,  Illinois Music Educators and Lawrence University’s Fred Sturm Jazz Festival. Her big band compositions are currently published by Sierra Music Publications, Doug Beach Music and Kendor Music. Having been selected to conduct the NAfME All-Eastern and All-Northwest Jazz Ensembles as well as All-State jazz ensembles throughout the country, she has also been an invited clinician at the National Association for Music Education Eastern Division Convention , International Society for Jazz Composition and Arranging Symposium and Jazz Education Network conferences.  She is on the Board of the International Society of Jazz Arrangers and Composers and also serves as the Coordinator for the JEN Sisters In Jazz Collegiate Combo Competition. Her quintet has performed at the San Jose Jazz Festival, Jazz Education Network Conference, Michigan Jazz Festival, Detroit International Jazz Festival and in jazz clubs around the country.
